chapters.title: Drift and when to choose Terraform

takeaways: Terraform declares infrastructure in readable files, so environments can be reviewed, reused and rebuilt instead of remembered.
The plan step shows exactly what will change before apply touches anything, and the state file is the memory that makes this comparison possible.
Keep state remote, locked and access-controlled, and treat drift as a team decision; for single-cloud Azure teams, Bicep can be the simpler choice.
hook: Portal clicks can't be rebuilt reliably, and that gap is why Terraform exists. This episode explains infrastructure as code, providers, plan and apply, state, modules and drift for anyone working with Azure or other clouds. You will be able to read a Terraform setup and know what it will do before it runs.
